records.claim: Remark 7.2 (counterexample to iterated Kochar-Xu conjecture at s = 2)
records.quote: Remark 7.2. ... Write, for simplicity, X = max{X1 , X2 } and Y = max{Y1 , Y2 } and consider Vs (x) = T̄ Y,s (x) − T̄ X,s (ax), where a > 0. If we choose the parameters (s, λ1 /λ2 , θ1 /θ2 , a) = (2, 0.34, 11, 2.89) the sign variation of Vs (x) is “−, +, −” so, according to Theorem 2.2, X and Y are not comparable with respect to the 2−IFRA order, hence they cannot be comparable with respect to the 2−IFR order. ... Indeed, taking into account the order relation (λ1 , λ2 ) ≺ (θ1 , θ2 ), it follows that (λ1 , λ2 , θ1 , θ2 ) = (1/1474)(408, 1200, 134, 1474)ϑ, with ϑ > 0, generates a whole family of counter-examples for the conjecture when the iteration parameter s = 2.
records.family: Two-component parallel systems of independent exponentials; rate vectors (lambda1,lambda2) majorized by (theta1,theta2) with lambda1+lambda2 = theta1+theta2 and lambda1 >= theta1
records.compared: X = max{X1,X2} vs Y = max{Y1,Y2} under majorized rate vectors

hypotheses.text: Kochar-Xu conjecture setup: (lambda1,...,lambdan) majorized by (theta1,...,thetan) should give max Xi <=1-IFR max Yi; here s=2, lambda1 <= lambda2, theta1 <= theta2, lambda1/lambda2 = 0.34, theta1/theta2 = 11, a = 2.89

conclusion.direction: X and Y are not comparable in the 2-IFRA order (sign variation of V_s is '-,+,-'), hence not comparable in the 2-IFR order — the iterated conjecture fails at s = 2

records.quantifiers: s = 2; n = 2; vartheta > 0 gives a family of counterexamples

records.quote: Theorem 2.3. Let X and Y be random variables with absolutely continuous distributions with densities fX and fY and distribution functions FX , FY ∈ F , respectively. If, for every constants a > 0 and b ∈ R, either of the functions, Hs (x) = (1/EY s−1 ) fY (x) − (as /EX s−1 ) fX (ax + b) or Hs−1 (x) = (1/EY s−1 ) F Y (x) − (as−1 /EX s−1 ) F X (ax + b), changes sign at most twice when x traverses from 0 to +∞, and if the change of sign occurs twice, it is in the order “+, −, +”, then FX ≤s−IFR FY . The functions Hs and Hs−1 may, respectively, be replaced by Ps (x) = log fY (x) − log fX (ax + b) + log(EX s−1 /(as EY s−1 )) and Ps−1 (x) = log F Y (x) − log F X (ax + b) + log(EX s−1 /(as−1 EY s−1 )).
